defects: Adds an extra hypothesis `[P.IsPrime]` on the base ideal (produced's `P`, matching gold's `p`) that gold does not require — gold's theorem only assumes primality of the ideal lying over (gold's `P.IsPrime`, matching produced's `Q.IsPrime`), leaving the base ideal `p` unconstrained in primality; the produced statement is therefore a strictly less general claim, not the same proposition.

The conclusion `FiniteDimensional.finrank (R ⧸ P) (S ⧸ Q)` requires a `Module (R ⧸ P) (S ⧸ Q)` instance to typecheck, but no such instance is derivable automatically from the plain Prop hypothesis `hlying : comap (algebraMap R S) Q = P` (unlike Mathlib's approach of building this via the `Ideal.LiesOver`/`inertiaDeg'` machinery, which explicitly constructs the algebra structure from the lying-over relation); as stated the term likely fails to elaborate.
